children: Oil and bond markets took center stage Thursday as renewed concern about a possible escalation between the United States and Iran pushed crude higher and encouraged investors to seek safety, while U.S. equities opened broadly lower.
The Nasdaq Composite lost 2% shortly after the opening bell, compared with declines of 0.7% for the S&P 500 and 0.4% for the Dow. Meta Platforms
dropped more than 5% despite beating quarterly estimates, and Tesla
fell more than 2% as investors digested its latest outlook and AI-related plans.

The pullback also reflected a tougher test for AI-related valuations. Investors have become less willing to reward large infrastructure budgets without clearer evidence that spending can produce durable returns, even as recent company results point to continued demand for AI services.

Energy prices moved in the opposite direction. Brent crude gained 3.3% to $112.43 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate rose 2.9% to $99.95. Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries attracted demand amid geopolitical uncertainty. French government bonds remained under pressure as investors weighed social unrest and concerns about the country's public finances.

title: Nasdaq Tumbles 2% as Meta and Tesla Fall and Oil Prices Surge
